Train a graph neural network

Source: R/graph-training.R
train_graph_model.Rd

A training loop for the common graph learning tasks. It uses the model, optimizer and loss as ordinary torch objects, so all of them stay accessible in the returned fit.

Usage

train_graph_model(
  model,
  data,
  task = c("node_classification", "node_regression", "graph_classification",
    "graph_regression", "link_prediction", "edge_classification", "edge_regression"),
  epochs = 100L,
  optimizer = "adam",
  lr = 0.01,
  weight_decay = 0,
  loss = NULL,
  val_data = NULL,
  batch_size = NULL,
  fanouts = NULL,
  decoder = NULL,
  scheduler = NULL,
  early_stopping = NULL,
  checkpoint_path = NULL,
  device = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  grad_clip = NULL,
  class_weights = NULL,
  target_type = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

model

An nn_module whose forward takes (x, edge_index, ...) with the named arguments documented in gnn_model().

data

Training data; see the table.

task

Prediction task.

epochs

Number of epochs.

optimizer

"adam", "adamw", "sgd", "rmsprop", "adagrad", or a function taking a parameter list and returning a torch optimizer.

lr

Learning rate.

weight_decay

L2 penalty passed to the optimizer.

loss

NULL for the task default (cross entropy, mean squared error, binary cross entropy with logits), a name ("cross_entropy", "mse", "l1", "huber", "bce", "focal"), or a function (prediction, target).

val_data

Validation graphs for graph level tasks.

batch_size

Graphs per batch (graph tasks) or seeds per batch (node tasks with fanouts).

fanouts

Neighbor sampling fanouts for node mini-batches.

decoder

Decoder module for link and edge tasks; defaults to link_decoder() "dot" and an edge_decoder().

scheduler

NULL, a list such as list(type = "step", step_size = 50, gamma = 0.5), list(type = "plateau", patience = 10, factor = 0.5) or list(type = "cosine"), or a function taking the optimizer and returning a torch scheduler.

early_stopping

Patience in epochs, or NULL to train all epochs. Monitors validation loss; the best weights are restored at the end.

checkpoint_path

Optional file; the model state is saved there with torch::torch_save() whenever validation loss improves.

device

Device, see graph_tensors().

seed

Optional integer seed.

grad_clip

Optional maximum gradient norm.

class_weights

Optional class weights for cross entropy.

target_type

Node type to predict for heterogeneous graphs.

verbose

Print progress every verbose epochs (FALSE for none).

Value

An object of class graph_fit.

Details

taskdatatargetsloss on
"node_classification", "node_regression"graph_data (or hetero_graph_data with target_type) with train_masknode ytraining nodes only
"graph_classification", "graph_regression"list of graph_data or a graph_dataset; val_data likewisegraph_yevery training graph
"link_prediction"a link_split from split_edges() (or split_edges_hetero())positive and sampled negative pairstraining pairs
"edge_classification", "edge_regression"graph_data with edge_y and masks from split_edge_labels()edge ytraining edges

Node mini-batches. With fanouts, node tasks are trained on sampled neighborhoods (node_loader()); the loss uses only the seed nodes of each batch, never the sampled context nodes. Validation uses the full graph.

Link prediction. Message passing uses split$train_graph, which holds training edges only. Fresh negative pairs are drawn every epoch, excluding training positives; validation and test pairs are never used for training.

Reproducibility. With seed, torch's global generator is seeded with torch_manual_seed(seed) (needed for weight initialization done before the call, and for dropout), and every R side random draw (batching, neighbor and negative sampling) uses a seed derived from seed inside withr::with_seed(), so the caller's R random state is not changed. The fit records seeds, settings, package versions and the device in fit$reproducibility. Training on GPUs may still be nondeterministic, because scatter additions on CUDA use atomic operations whose order is not fixed.

Examples

if (torch::torch_is_installed()) {
  g <- split_nodes(dataset_karate(), seed = 1)
  model <- gnn_model("sage", input_dim = num_node_features(g),
                     hidden_dim = 16, output_dim = 2)
  fit <- train_graph_model(model, g, "node_classification", epochs = 30,
                           seed = 1)
  fit
  head(predict(fit, g))
}
